en: Part one, notes from the curve.
zh: 第一部分,来自 The Curve 的笔记。

speaker: Unknown
en: Last weekend, I was at the curve at Light Haven in Berkeley.
zh: 上周末,我在伯克利 Light Haven 的 The Curve 会议。

speaker: Unknown
en: Prakash asked about me laying out the divides I saw.
zh: Prakash 问到我,让我阐述我所看到的分歧。

en: One of the big observations in general in AI is that events have come pretty fast and you would think if you were looking back, you know, if you were looking ahead a couple of years ago that

speaker: Unknown
en: With two years of additional information and revelations and actually seeing how strong the AIs get and what they do and who's been right or wrong, you would think that people would start to agree on the state of things.
zh: 有了两年的额外信息、揭示,以及实际看到 AI 变得多强、它们做什么、谁对谁错,你会认为人们会开始就事物的状态达成一致。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that has happened a lot less in the broader world than I would have expected.
zh: 而这在我更广阔的世界里发生得比我预期的少得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I did feel that there was some of that felt at the curve.
zh: 但我确实感到,在 The Curve 上有那么一些这种感觉。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I do think the big thing that people have kind of come together on, at least to a significant degree, is
zh: 但我确实认为,人们已经大体达成一致的重大事情,至少在相当程度上,是

speaker: Unknown
en: It does look like the AIs are going to get really powerful and this is something we're really going to have to reckon with and can't just sort of hope goes away or, you know, feel like maybe if we just wait, you know, the bubble will burst or the fever will break or what have you.
zh: 看起来 AI 确实会变得非常强大,这是我们真的必须认真对待的事情,不能只是指望它会消失,或者,你知道,觉得也许只要等等,泡沫就会破裂,或者热度就会退去,诸如此类。

speaker: Unknown
en: This time around, people were definitely like, okay, it's getting pretty serious.
zh: 这一次,人们肯定是在说,好,事情变得相当严肃了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, there were very few perspectives that
zh: 你知道,很少有那样的观点了——

speaker: Unknown
en: As Helen Toner once famously put it, long timelines have got super short.
zh: 正如 Helen Toner 曾经著名地说过的,长timeline变得超级短。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would say another corollary to that was what is called normal in terms of expectations is getting increasingly pretty incredible.
zh: 我想说的另一个推论是,所谓的「正常」预期正在变得越来越不可思议。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would say the people there who had the most modest expectations for what AIs will be able to do were like
zh: 我想说的是,在那里对 AI 能力预期最温和的人也像是——

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, it's going to do an awful lot.
zh: 是啊,它将会做到非常多的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the question now on the capabilities front has gone to like, is RSI going to foom?
zh: 而现在能力方面的问题已经变成,比如,RSI 会不会 foom?

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it going to be fast for a while and then kind of level off?
zh: 会不会是快上一阵子,然后趋于平缓?

speaker: Unknown
en: Is that more than it's meant to be?
zh: 它是不是比它本来的意义更多?

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, yeah, we've got these super powerful things, but is it really going to kind of run away from us?
zh: 比如,是的,我们有了这些超级强大的东西,但它真的会失控地跑掉吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Those are still the capabilities questions that we're getting asked.
zh: 这些仍然是我们在被问到的能力问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: But there has been, I think, some healthy updating across the community just based on what we've seen.
zh: 但我认为,仅仅基于我们所看到的,整个社群已经有了一些健康的更新。

speaker: Unknown
en: Prakash asked whether anyone from the Frontier Labs said limits should be enforced on the players in this space, themselves included?
zh: Prakash 问,是否有来自前沿实验室的人说应该对这一领域的参与者——包括他们自己在内——实施限制?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, that was a huge topic.
zh: 是的,那是一个巨大的话题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, and probably the biggest divide in terms of perspective is really just inside the Frontier companies, outside the Frontier companies, right?
zh: 我的意思是,观点上最大的分歧可能真的就是前沿公司内部与前沿公司外部,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Everybody knows that they're living in the future and they have visibility that the rest of us don't have.
zh: 每个人都知道他们活在未来,他们有我们其他人所没有的可见性。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so actually I had a chance to talk to and hear from, in some cases in sessions, in some cases just in, you know, passing conversations, all Chatham House rules will all abstract away.
zh: 所以实际上我有机会与一些人交谈并聆听他们，有时是在会议上，有时只是在随意的交谈中，一切都是查塔姆守则，都会抽象掉。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we're talking people who are like founders, executives, top researchers at Frontier companies and, you know, a small set of them.
zh: 但我们说的是那些创始人、高管、前沿公司的顶级研究员，而且只是一小部分人。

speaker: Unknown
en: I asked a couple of them.
zh: 我问了他们中的几个人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why come here?
zh: 为什么来这里？

speaker: Unknown
en: What's in it for you?
zh: 对你们有什么好处？

speaker: Unknown
en: And before doing a couple of sessions where I was interviewing or moderating, I asked the same question, what makes this next hour a good use of your time?
zh: 在我进行几个采访或主持的环节之前，我问了同样的问题，是什么让接下来这一小时成为对你时间的良好利用？

speaker: Unknown
en: And they repeatedly expressed that it's just important to them to share as much as they can with the broader community.
zh: 他们反复表示，尽其所能与更广泛的社区分享对他们来说很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: Definitely not sharing their trade secrets, of course, still, but really trying to give us a candid take on what are they seeing internally?
zh: 当然，肯定不是分享他们的商业机密，但确实是想给我们坦诚地讲讲他们内部在看到什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What do they believe internally?
zh: 他们内部相信什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What's their outlook?
zh: 他们的展望是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What's the plan?
zh: 计划是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: How can we come together and potentially do some of these constraints?
zh: 我们如何能聚在一起，潜在地解决其中一些限制？

speaker: Unknown
en: And there were a number of things that I actually thought were kind of newsworthy.
zh: 而且有一些事情我认为其实挺有新闻价值的。

speaker: Unknown
en: One, let's say, senior executive at a frontier lab
zh: 一位，比如说，前沿实验室的资深高管

speaker: Unknown
en: First of all was saying that just pre-training continues to deliver, that the models are just at the base level of capability, getting stronger and stronger.
zh: 首先表示，预训练持续有效，模型在基础能力层面上正变得越来越好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it doesn't seem to be an obvious stopping point to that.
zh: 而且似乎没有一个明显的停止点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Scaling laws are holding or maybe even bending because the data quality is getting better.
zh: 缩放定律依然成立，甚至可能正在弯曲，因为数据质量在变好。

speaker: Unknown
en: They've got increasingly different architecture tricks, lots of work on synthetic data.
zh: 他们有了越来越不同的架构技巧，在合成数据上做了大量工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Synthetic data seems to be definitely really delivering.
zh: 合成数据显然确实非常有效。

speaker: Unknown
en: Basically, you need more pre-training data.
zh: 基本上，你需要更多预训练数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: What do you do?
zh: 你怎么办？

speaker: Unknown
en: You give the model a bunch of data and think, what could I transform this data into that if I then pre-trained on it would make the model smarter?
zh: 你给模型一大堆数据，然后想，我能把这些数据转化成什么，使得如果我之后用它们预训练，会让模型更聪明？

speaker: Unknown
en: And you're converting these reasoning tokens, your test time compute, you're converting back into pre-training data, which then goes in, of course, to the next generation of models.
zh: 你在把这些推理 token、你的测试时计算，转换回预训练数据，这些数据当然会进入下一代模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is one way in which recursive self-improvement is happening.
zh: 这是递归自我改进正在发生的一种方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: Not even necessarily, there are, of course, opportunities for architectural improvements as well, but a big emphasis was just on data quality.
zh: 甚至不一定，当然也有机遇进行架构改进，但很大的重点放在了数据质量上。

speaker: Unknown
en: We can now just spend tokens on the existing data to augment it, to create better, cleaner, different lenses on it.
zh: 我们现在可以在现有数据上花 token 来增强它，创造出更好的、更干净的、不同视角的数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: We feed all that back in and the models get better.
zh: 我们把所有这些反馈进去，模型就变好了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this one executive was really emphasizing pre-training, continues to deliver, the models are getting super powerful.
zh: 所以这位高管特别强调，预训练持续有效，模型正变得超级强大。

speaker: Unknown
en: RL is important too, but
zh: RL 也很重要，但是

speaker: Unknown
en: His take actually went as far as he believes that the latest frontier models do have the ineffable research taste that would be needed for them to start making paradigm level breakthroughs.
zh: 他的看法实际上走得非常远，他相信最新的前沿模型确实拥有那种开始做出范式级别突破所需要的难以言传的研究品味。

speaker: Unknown
en: He believes it's currently an elicitation problem where the RL is not bringing it out well enough.
zh: 他相信这目前是一个引出的问题，即 RL 没有把它足够好地引出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: They don't know quite how to bring it out well enough.
zh: 他们还不太知道如何把它足够好地引出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it's kind of rare.
zh: 所以它有点稀少。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is why you need 10,000 agents to do a Millennium Prize problem.
zh: 而这就是为什么你需要 1 万个智能体去解决一个千禧年大奖难题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And of course that's verifiable too.
zh: 当然那个也是可验证的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So like RL is working better there.
zh: 所以 RL 在那里效果更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe you need a million agents, you know, at this point to like stumble onto something eventually where you'd get the kind of paradigmatic change at a, you know, ML research level.
zh: 也许你现在需要 100 万个智能体，来最终偶然发现一些东西，让你获得 ML 研究层面上那种范式性的变革。

speaker: Unknown
en: But he believes that is there and it will be, they'll figure out how to elicit it.
zh: 但他相信那是存在的，而且他们会想出如何把它引出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then he said a couple of things that I thought were just like legitimately newsworthy.
zh: 然后他说了几件事，我觉得真的确实有新闻价值。

speaker: Unknown
en: One was
zh: 其一是

speaker: Unknown
en: He believes that there is a level of intelligence or there is might be a little strong, but there, there likely is, let's say a level of intelligence that we just shouldn't go past.
zh: 他相信存在一种智能水平，或者说可能有这一点有点强，但是，很可能存在，比如说一种我们不应该越过的智能水平。

speaker: Unknown
en: What?
zh: 什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: First time I'd ever heard that from a frontier lab leader.
zh: 这是我第一次从一位前沿实验室领导者那里听到这种说法。

speaker: Unknown
en: Um, and it was not like minced words.
zh: 嗯，而且不是含糊其辞。

speaker: Unknown
en: It wasn't a, like, there's definitely a level or I can articulate what that level is, but like,
zh: 不是那种，比如说，肯定有一个水平，或者我能说清楚那个水平是什么，而是，

speaker: Unknown
en: This was a person who, again, like everybody would recognize their name and position saying,
zh: 这是一个，再说一次，每个人都能认出其名字和职位的人，他说，

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it is likely that there's a level that we shouldn't go past.
zh: 我认为很可能存在一个我们不应该越过的水平。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, was that not ever or just, you know, not right now?
zh: 那么，那不是永远不做，还是只是，你知道，现在不做？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that was also a little bit ambiguous, but it was a pretty firm statement, definitely the strongest statement I've heard about imposing kind of a hard cap on capabilities, even for a time.
zh: 我觉得那也有点模糊，但这是一个相当坚定的声明，绝对是关于施加某种能力硬上限的最强声明，即使只是暂时的。

speaker: Unknown
en: What confuses me about that statement is that some of the increases in intelligence that we were seeing
zh: 让我对这个说法感到困惑的是，我们正在看到的一些智能提升

speaker: Unknown
en: Number one, they're coming as a result of compute, increases in compute, which has traditionally been what has happened in the last decade and a half.
zh: 第一，它们是算力的结果，算力的增长，而这传统上就是过去十五年里一直在发生的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Number two, they are coming as a result of refining the input data.
zh: 第二，它们是对输入数据进行优化的结果。

speaker: Unknown
en: The input data is being refined by greater intelligences, and so you have input data, which is much better.
zh: 输入数据正在被更强大的智能所优化，所以你得到的输入数据要好得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: When we say that we shouldn't go exceed a point of intelligence, that automatically means that you have to look at the inputs going in.
zh: 当我们说不应该超过某个智能水平时，这自动意味着你必须审视投入的输入。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the inputs going in are going to be compute and this refinement of data.
zh: 而投入的输入将是算力和这种数据优化。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if you say that we shouldn't go beyond that point, that also means that you shouldn't build compute beyond that point, or you shouldn't refine data further beyond that point, which means a lot, really.
zh: 所以如果你说我们不应该超过那个点，那也意味着你不应该在那一点之上继续建设算力，或者不应该在那一点之上进一步优化数据，这意义重大，真的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It means like the end of the compute build-out, which is pretty significant, right?
zh: 它意味着算力建设的终结，这是相当重大的，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, well, I don't know.
zh: 是啊，嗯，我不知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I think there's a lot of uses for compute.
zh: 我是说，我认为算力有很多用途。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I had a chance to follow up on this combination of
zh: 所以我有机会跟进这个组合：

speaker: Unknown
en: Pre-training is really delivering and scaling laws.
zh: 预训练确实在兑现承诺，还有缩放定律。

speaker: Unknown
en: If anything, maybe you're bending more favorably.
zh: 如果有什么变化的话，也许曲线正朝着更有利的方向弯曲。

speaker: Unknown
en: Although it's tricky to know what you count, right?
zh: 虽然很难知道该怎么计算，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you count all those flops that you use to create the synthetic data?
zh: 你要把那些用来创建合成数据的 flops 都算进去吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe you should.
zh: 也许应该算。

speaker: Unknown
en: How to count these things is always super vexing.
zh: 如何计算这些东西总是非常令人头疼。

speaker: Unknown
en: But between this pre-training thing and there might be a cap on how far we should go that I just asked to follow up like, okay, well, how do we operationalize that?
zh: 但在这个预训练问题和可能存在一个我们应该走多远的上限之间，我只是追问了一句：好，那我们怎么把它落地？

speaker: Unknown
en: Would you be prepared to sign on to something like

en: I'll limit on the number of flops that go into the next pre-training run.

en: You know, should we say, and I don't know what that number would be, but, and again, what exactly would count, but like, should we say no more than 10 to the 27 flops in the next pre-train or something like that?
zh: 你知道，我们是否应该说——我不知道那个数字是多少，而且同样，具体什么算数也不清楚——但比如说，我们是否应该说下一次预训练不超过 10 的 27 次方 flops 之类的？

speaker: Unknown
en: And I kind of anticipated that being a bit of like a straw man for him to react to or like tell me what was bad about that and maybe ideally give me a better idea.
zh: 我有点预料到这对他来说会像是个稻草人，让他来回应，或者告诉我这有什么不好的地方，最好能给我一个更好的主意。

speaker: Unknown
en: But what actually happened was he basically said, yeah, I think that could be reasonable.
zh: 但实际发生的是，他基本上说，是啊，我觉得那可能是合理的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The end, not really much of a fight there at all.
zh: 就这样，根本没有多少争论。

speaker: Unknown
en: As reported by analysts, NVIDIA for the next generation is actually cutting down the memory capacity because of costs and everything involved.
zh: 正如分析师报道的,NVIDIA 下一代由于成本以及相关的一切,实际上在削减内存容量。

speaker: Unknown
en: So they're only going to be at 192 gigabytes with the Rubin Ultra.
zh: 所以 Rubin Ultra 只会达到 192 GB。

speaker: Unknown
en: But even if you use that 288 as the current benchmark,
zh: 但即使你用那个 288 作为当前的基准,

speaker: Unknown
en: We've got eight times more memory capacity per chip.
zh: 我们每颗芯片的内存容量是它的 8 倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that means on a per chip basis, you now can actually scale in what you would have needed from a memory perspective, eight GPUs for, we can do on a single device.
zh: 所以这意味着在单芯片的基础上,你现在实际上可以做到,从内存角度原本需要 8 块 GPU 才能实现的事情,我们在单个设备上就能做到。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's not just, oh, you've got that cost silicon savings, you know, as you pointed out, whenever you have to scale to having more than one device.
zh: 而且这不仅仅是,哦,你节省了硅片成本,你知道,正如你指出的,每当你必须扩展到超过一个设备时,

speaker: Unknown
en: There's overheads involved with that.
zh: 都会有开销牵涉其中。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's your all-gathers, all-reduces that you have to do for each layer and really each multiply that you're doing of sharding across those devices.
zh: 有那些你在每一层都要做的 all-gathers、all-reduces,实际上你在这些设备上做的每一次分片乘法都要做。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then I asked Tom about looping, where a model runs the same layers more than once for each token, and why that is tempting at all.
zh: 接着我问了 Tom 关于循环(looping)的问题,也就是一个模型对每个 token 多次运行相同的层,以及为什么这根本就有吸引力。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's been very interesting from the Loop Transformers paper to that being the rumor of one of the big advancements with the GPT-6 Astra.
zh: 从 Loop Transformers 论文,到它成为 GPT-6 Astra 重大进展之一的传闻,这一直都非常有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: Simply repeating the forward path gets you that improvement, but it's crazy that there is
zh: 简单地重复前向路径就能带来那种提升,但疯狂的是,确实有

speaker: Unknown
en: Really work that I think was only being done in sort of the fringes of the open source, you know, transformer community, you know, two, three years ago of taking like a Llama 7DB and just duplicating layers within it.
zh: 我认为在两三年前,这种工作只出现在开源 transformer 社区的边缘地带,比如拿一个 Llama 7DB,直接在它内部复制层。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it was taking like a 7DB model.
zh: 也就是拿一个 7DB 模型,

speaker: Unknown
en: And slightly strategically saying, okay, I'm going to just repeat these sets of map models in sequence and turning it into like a hundred billion parameter model.
zh: 然后稍微有点策略地说,好,我就要把这些 map models 按顺序重复,把它变成一个一千亿参数的模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you got better results from it, even though it was repeating the exact same map models.
zh: 然后你从中得到了更好的结果,即使它重复的是完全相同的 map models。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there is an element- Imagine what you can do when you train it to work that way.
zh: 所以确实有一个因素——想象一下,当你训练它以那种方式工作时,你能做到什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Exactly.
zh: 正是如此。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you already have very high confidence on what the next token is going to be and multiple layers have agreed on that, decide to early exit and go out.
zh: 如果你已经对下一个 token 会是什么有很高的置信度,而且多个层都已达成一致,那就决定提前退出、直接输出。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or if you're really uncertain about something, actually find which layers in the network actually will have a higher likelihood of being able to increase that probability.
zh: 或者,如果你对某件事真的不确定,那就实际找出网络中哪些层更有可能提高那个概率。

speaker: Unknown
en: Same sort of like functions that the MLD router does in terms of determining which experts should be selected on a per token basis.
zh: 这和 MLD 路由器所做的功能类似,也就是在每个 token 的基础上决定应该选择哪些专家。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you extend that concept to, okay, if you're really unsure if there's a very large set of equally weighted probabilities for what the next token should be in your three-quarters of the way through the layer,
zh: 如果你把这个概念扩展一下,好,如果你真的不确定,在 layer 走到四分之三的地方时,对于下一个 token 应该是什么,存在一个非常大的、权重均等的概率集合,

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you actually just want to route back and determine, okay, we actually need a different set of experts, something like for this.
zh: 你是否真的想要路由回去,决定,好,我们实际上需要一组不同的专家,类似这样的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I wouldn't be surprised if these things are already being done at scale in the major model lines.
zh: 但如果这些事情已经在主要模型产品线中大规模实践了,我也不会感到惊讶。

speaker: Unknown
en: But can you go just a little bit farther into the hardware connection of that?
zh: 但你能再稍微深入讲一下它与硬件的联系吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Because I'm kind of coming in with assumptions along the lines of, you know, just very fundamental terms, like why loop at all?
zh: 因为我带着一些假设进来,用非常基础的术语来说,就是为什么要循环?

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it has to do with this kind of memory bandwidth, right?
zh: 我认为这和这种内存带宽有关,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Because now I can keep the same weights on the chip and I don't have to like shuffle things in and out as much.
zh: 因为现在我可以把相同的权重留在芯片上,我不需要那么频繁地把东西搬进搬出。

speaker: Unknown
en: No.
zh: 不。

speaker: Unknown
en: Not really, because within, when, basically the assumption is, if you're doing inference, that you're going to have all of your weights locally in DRAM, you're just sharding that over some number of devices.
zh: 不完全是,因为在——基本上假设是,如果你在做推理,你所有的权重都会在本地 DRAM 里,你只是把它分片到一定数量的设备上。

speaker: Unknown
en: You do get some amortization, but just with the size of experts and the size of caches on chips, there's not much of a reuse opportunity, or by the time you're already done with the layer, you've already gone through the amount of memory many times that of what is in like the on-chip SRAMs.
zh: 你确实能得到一些摊销,但就专家的规模和芯片上缓存的规模而言,没有多少复用的机会,或者等你做完这一层时,你已经多次遍历了相当于片上 SRAM 容量很多倍的内存量。

speaker: Unknown
en: From a hardware perspective, looping really is more memory capacity savings than memory bandwidth savings.
zh: 从硬件角度来看,循环真正节省的更多是内存容量,而不是内存带宽。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because let's say that you trained two models with the same base set, and you trained one to do with looping, and so it only has 10 layers instead of 20 layers.
zh: 因为假设你用同一个基础集合训练了两个模型,你训练其中一个使用循环,所以它只有 10 层而不是 20 层。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Model B is 20 layers.
zh: 而 Model B 是 20 层。

speaker: Unknown
en: That 20-layer model...
zh: 那个 20 层的模型……

speaker: Unknown
en: Doing very, very simple is going to be double the size of the 10 layer version.
zh: 用非常非常简单的方式来说,会是 10 层版本的两倍大小。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you find that the linked 10 layer version gets 95% of the same quality of results and it's half the size, you're probably going to deploy that one.
zh: 而且如果你发现那个带链接的 10 层版本达到了 95% 的相同质量结果,而且只有一半大小,你很可能会部署那一个。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're saving more capacity than bandwidth.
zh: 你节省的容量比带宽多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because doing the second loop, you still have to do the same memory fetches and do all of the same number of mapmoles.
zh: 因为做第二次循环时,你仍然要做同样的内存读取,做同样次数的 mapmoles。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's the exact same number of bytes that need to be moved and the exact same number of flops that have to be done in that Model A and Model B scenario.
zh: 在那个 Model A 和 Model B 的场景里,需要移动的字节数完全相同,需要执行的 flops 数量也完全相同。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just that Model B, the 20 layers, actually has unique different weights for the second group of 10 layers that have to be done.
zh: 只不过是 Model B,那 20 层,实际上第二组 10 层拥有不同的、独有的权重需要执行。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that means you require twice the memory capacity.
zh: 而这就意味着你需要两倍的内存容量。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then I turned to how AI is changing chip development itself.
zh: 接着我转向了 AI 如何改变芯片开发本身。

zh: 在 Jensen Huang 最近接受 Ezra Klein 的一次著名访谈中,他谈到 NVIDIA 大约把 20% 的时间和精力用于设计,然后 80% 用于验证、确认、确保长寿命、可靠性,等等等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: What do your ratios look like on that?
zh: 你们的比率看起来是怎样的?

speaker: Unknown
en: So for us, I would say it's a little bit different because we're starting from scratch.
zh: 对我们来说,我觉得有点不同,因为我们是从零开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's a lot more like base layer, base capability design that we have to start from scratch.
zh: 所以有更多的底层、基础能力的设计需要我们从零开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: So for our first full custom silicon, Osimov, it was about a...
zh: 所以对我们的第一块全定制芯片 Osimov,大概是……

speaker: Unknown
en: It will end up being somewhere around maybe 60% design focus for us to 40% verification.
zh: 最终大概会是接近 60% 的设计投入,对 40% 的验证。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would say like the most amazing thing that I don't think would have been possible three or six months ago and only really became possible with GPT-6 Astra and now Opus 5.5 that we're leveraging a lot in this task is
zh: 我想说,最令人惊叹的、我认为在三或六个月前不可能实现、只有随着 GPT-6 Astra 以及现在 Opus 5.5 才真正成为可能——我们在这项任务中大量利用了它们——的事情是

speaker: Unknown
en: For doing our verification work, we use Cadence, Pleiadian emulator systems.
zh: 在做验证工作时,我们使用 Cadence 的 Pleiadian 仿真器系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: These are big, giant racks that are full of custom ASICs that are specifically designed to just emulate, do gate-level emulation of silicon.
zh: 这些是装满定制 ASIC 的大型巨型机架,那些 ASIC 是专门设计用来做仿真的,即对硅片做门级仿真。

speaker: Unknown
en: The crazy thing about Astra and Opus 5.5 is this fact that...
zh: Astra 和 Opus 5.5 的疯狂之处在于这样一个事实……

speaker: Unknown
en: The agents themselves have been able to completely do closed loop iteration and testing on this.
zh: 智能体本身已经能够在上面完成完全闭环的迭代和测试。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think people thought it was crazy, but handing these very powerful agents full keys to our internal infrastructure and saying,
zh: 我觉得人们当时认为这很疯狂,但把这些非常强大的智能体交给我们内部基础设施的完整钥匙,并说,

speaker: Unknown
en: Here's a Palladium piece.
zh: 这是一台 Palladium 设备。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I highly doubt that these models had Palladium documentation in their retraining thing, especially because a lot of documents are new as software updates.
zh: 而且我非常怀疑这些模型在它们的再训练数据里有 Palladium 的文档,尤其是因为很多文档都是随软件更新才有的新内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the fact that it went and looked up the documentation when we're looking at these agent traces, the reasoning traces and tool calls, et cetera, it's reading the full documentation, effectively compressing that itself by reading the PDFs.
zh: 但事实是,当我们查看这些智能体的轨迹、推理轨迹和工具调用等等时,发现它去查阅了完整文档,通过阅读 PDF 有效地自行压缩了那些内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: Generating its own, you know, markdown files of cheat sheets of what to do, and then building out all of the testing infrastructure in its own harnesses for being able to access this.
zh: 生成它自己的、你知道的、关于该做什么的速查表 markdown 文件，然后构建它自己的所有测试基础设施和测试框架以便能够访问这些内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's mind-blowing.
zh: 这太令人震撼了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so while if you're just doing regular software RTL simulation, that's running on the order of like 10 hertz for us in those cases.
zh: 所以如果你只是做常规的软件 RTL 仿真，在这些情况下它的运行速度大约是 10 赫兹的量级。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you remove a lot of the debug...
zh: 如果你移除很多拖慢速度的调试……

speaker: Unknown
en: pieces that slow things down, etc.
zh: 那些部分等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: We can run the full chip emulation on the order of 500 kHz.
zh: 我们可以以 500 kHz 的量级运行完整芯片仿真。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you've got actually several orders of magnitude speed up an improvement from that gate-level hardware piece, and this just gets us closer to this RSI loop.
zh: 所以你实际上从那个门级硬件部分获得了好几个数量级的速度提升和改进，而这只是让我们更接近这个 RSI 循环。

speaker: Unknown
en: And right now that's really just focused on implementing test programs.
zh: 现在这真的只是专注于实现测试程序。

speaker: Unknown
en: Finding cases where they fail, and then writing out reports, which get reviewed by other agents and by humans in the loop.
zh: 找到它们失败的情况，然后写出报告，这些报告会被其他智能体和处于流程中的人类审阅。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I would say when this really started working, six weeks ago, roughly, beginning of September when Astra 6 came out.
zh: 但我想说，当这一切真正开始生效时，大约六周前，九月初，Astra 6 发布的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was a huge step function improvement from GPT 5.6, where...
zh: 相对于 GPT 5.6，这是一个巨大的阶跃函数式改进，而……

speaker: Unknown
en: It could not do that full closed loop itself.
zh: 它自己无法完成那个完整的闭环。

speaker: Unknown
en: It still required humans at different stages.
zh: 它在不同阶段仍然需要人类。

en: I asked how Positron's spending on AI compares with its spending on people.
zh: 我问 Positron 在 AI 上的支出与在人力上的支出相比如何。

speaker: Unknown
en: So on the token spend side, it's become our single largest non-manufacturing line item very quickly.
zh: 所以在 token 支出方面，它很快成为我们最大的非制造类支出项目。

speaker: Unknown
en: Bigger than human salaries.
zh: 比人类工资还大。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, just recently.
zh: 是的，就在最近。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's interesting.
zh: 而且这很有意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: It eclipsed human salaries.
zh: 它超过了人类工资。

zh: 然后又降下来了。

zh: 我一会儿解释。

zh: 所以，是的，我们的 token 支出大幅增加，嗯，好吧，六个月前它还相当于一名员工的水平。

speaker: Unknown
en: In, in June, it started to now be multiple employees.
zh: 在，在六月，它开始变成相当于多名员工的水平。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, we, we were peaking, you know, in the, in the days after GPT success, we're really trying to, to push its boundaries, et cetera.
zh: 比如，我们，我们在，你知道，在 GPT 成功之后的那些天里达到了峰值，我们真的在努力，努力推动它的边界等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're, we're spending over a hundred thousand dollars a day on tokens.
zh: 我们，我们每天在 token 上花费超过十万美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: That tempered down a little bit in the weeks after as we optimized a bit and just weren't trying to run as many parallel experiments.
zh: 在那之后的几周里，这个数字稍微降温了一些，因为我们做了一些优化，只是不再尝试运行那么多并行实验。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I would say the big thing that was like a saving grace was Opus 5.5 came out, and in a lot of our tests, not everything, it was doing better than Astra and was a quarter the price.
zh: 但我想说，最大的一个救星是 Opus 5.5 发布了，在我们的很多测试中（不是全部），它表现得比 Astra 更好，而价格只有四分之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: We didn't tell anyone to cut their spending or do anything, even though we were seeing this exponential growth in our token spend.
zh: 我们没有让任何人削减支出或做任何事情，即使我们看到了 token 支出的指数级增长。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was really just the fact that we both
zh: 真的只是因为我们俩都

speaker: Unknown
en: Felt that we were getting good ROI on it, so we weren't going to taper it.
zh: 觉得我们从中获得了不错的投资回报，所以我们不打算缩减它。

speaker: Unknown
en: But personally, my philosophy is I really don't want anyone to be running a real software or hardware development task on anything that is less than the best model.
zh: 但就我个人而言，我的理念是我真的不希望任何人在任何低于最佳模型的东西上运行真正的软件或硬件开发任务。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't care if it's a tenth of the cost per token.
zh: 我不在乎它是不是只有十分之一的每 token 成本。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just not worth the expense.
zh: 这就是不值得的花费。

zh: Prakash 问 Tom 是否见过 AI 在芯片设计中提出真正出乎意料的想法，而不是遵循手册里的规则？

speaker: Unknown
en: I have not yet.
zh: 我还没有见过。

en: I would say that's the most disappointing elements of all.
zh: 我想说这是所有事情中最令人失望的部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: As you can probably tell, I think all of this is insanely amazing and I think we're going to continue this exponential trend.
zh: 正如你可能看出来的，我认为这一切都极其惊人，而且我认为我们会继续这个指数级趋势。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm somewhat proud of the fact that it has not figured out some of
zh: 我在某种程度上感到骄傲的是，它还没有弄清楚我们所做的某些

speaker: Unknown
en: Our cleverness of what we've done, like it's it has questioned and like this seems like a bad design decision until it gets explained to it why something's done or it actually runs test and sees and understands oh that's why you're not doing the traditional way a systolic array is done.
zh: 巧妙之处，比如它质疑过，比如这看起来像是一个糟糕的设计决策，直到有人向它解释为什么这么做，或者它实际运行测试并看到并理解，哦，这就是为什么你没有按照传统的方式去做脉动阵列。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do I think that will hold for another six months?
zh: 我是否认为这种情况还能再持续六个月？

speaker: Unknown
en: Not sure, but just because in part why I actually think it's not going to be like the agent will come up with a better idea immediately.
zh: 不确定，但部分原因是我其实认为它不会是这样的，比如智能体会立刻想出一个更好的主意。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the amazing turn of events that we've just had in the past few weeks in terms of us having access to these models is the fact that just because it can iterate so fast and do experiments and things by itself,
zh: 我认为过去几周我们刚刚经历的惊人转折，就我们能够使用这些模型而言，正是它能够迭代得如此之快、自己进行实验等等这一事实，

speaker: Unknown
en: I wouldn't be surprised if it would come to the same conclusions we did, or maybe make better things than what we would do by ourselves, just because it's going to be able to iterate so fast and go through so many different design possibilities.
zh: 如果它得出和我们一样的结论，或者也许做出比我们自己会做的更好的东西，我不会感到惊讶，只是因为它将能够迭代得如此之快，尝试如此多不同的设计可能性。

speaker: Unknown
en: OpenAI solving Navigator Stokes, like the same approach of, yeah, if you take 10,000 agents and send them off for millions of man-years worth of effort, they found a solution.

speaker: Unknown
en: I asked how software engineers are feeling right now, empowered or threatened?
zh: 我问软件工程师们现在感觉如何，是被赋能了还是被威胁了？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I think college kids are a bit worried.
zh: 是的,我觉得大学生们有点担心。

speaker: Unknown
en: But other than that, if you're relatively plugged in and very capable of AI engineering tooling, you're in more demand than you've ever been because your expected value is higher than it's ever been.
zh: 但除此之外,如果你相对紧跟潮流,并且非常擅长 AI 工程工具,那么你现在比以往任何时候都更抢手,因为你的期望价值比以往任何时候都高。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this is definitely one of those Jevon's Paradox type things where
zh: 所以这绝对是那种杰文斯悖论(Jevon's Paradox)类型的事情,

speaker: Unknown
en: The sort of cost of software, creating software has gone down, therefore the demand has increased a lot, but for a very specific kind of demand for people who can manage coding agents productively instead of producing a whole bunch of slop.
zh: 也就是创造软件的成本降低了,因此需求大幅增加,但这是针对一种非常特定的需求,即能够高效管理编码智能体、而不是产出一大堆垃圾(slop)的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I've been in that situation, so I am both an engineer but also an employer of
zh: 而我自己就处于这种境地,所以我既是工程师,同时也是

speaker: Unknown
en: Engineers and people who are not engineers who are bi-coding.
zh: 而这不是那么关于经验的年限。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the phrase I've sort of recently taken to is, I don't want to pay for someone else to go through LLM psychosis, right?
zh: 我最近常挂在嘴边的一句话是:我不想付钱让别人去经历 LLM 精神错乱,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: I can pay for my own psychosis, that's fine.
zh: 我可以为自己付钱经历精神错乱,那没问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: But when you work for me and I'm paying your tokens, you better be actually producing thoughtful stuff.
zh: 但当你为我工作、我为你付 token 费用时,你最好是真的在产出有思想深度的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I have two or three employees right now who are basically under performance review because they're just giving me Claude Slop.
zh: 我现在有两三个员工基本上处于绩效考核状态,因为他们给我的就是 Claude 垃圾(Claude Slop)。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's really bad for them.
zh: 这对他们来说真的很糟糕。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they don't understand it.
zh: 而且他们不理解这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: They don't see it.
zh: 他们看不出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're like, what do you mean?
zh: 他们会说:你什么意思?

speaker: Unknown
en: I think this is perfectly fine.
zh: 我觉得这完全没问题啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm like, well, you're not producing any value.
zh: 然后我就说:你没在产出任何价值。

speaker: Unknown
en: I can just prompt Claude.
zh: 我自己直接 prompt Claude 就行了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't need you.
zh: 我不需要你。

speaker: Unknown
en: I asked whether years of coding experience still matter when he hires or whether product sense and high standards matter more.
zh: 我问他,在招聘时多年编程经验是否仍然重要,还是产品感和高标准更重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't care so much except for, let's call it security roles and for anything sort of backend, scalability.
zh: 我不太在乎经验,除了所谓的安全岗位,以及任何涉及后端、可扩展性的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: I just recorded an interview with the Superbase founders who are scaling Postgres to a scale that we've never seen before.
zh: 我刚录了一期和 Superbase 创始人的访谈,他们把 Postgres 扩展到了我们从未见过的规模。

speaker: Unknown
en: Good luck trying to hire somebody to scale Postgres with a complete self-managed sharding solution that works at YouTube scale.
zh: 祝你好运,想招一个能把 Postgres 用完全自管的分片方案扩展到 YouTube 规模的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's only one person in the world that can do that, and then they hired the guy.
zh: 世界上只有一个人能做到这一点,然后他们把那个人招到了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, you better go and, you know, make sure you don't lose data, that you, like, don't have, don't cause downtime, that you scale economically, because basically agents consume databases, something like at a 500 to 1 ratio of what human developers do.
zh: 就是说,你最好确保不丢数据、不造成停机、能经济地扩展,因为智能体消耗数据库的量,差不多是人类开发者的 500 比 1。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then, yeah, so, like, other than that, like, you can mostly vibe code, and then it is about taste.
zh: 那么,是的,除此之外,你基本可以 vibe code,而这讲究的就是品味。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's not so much about length of experience.
zh: 这其实和经验长短关系不大。

speaker: Unknown
en: Actually, sometimes length of experience works against you because you just have a set way of doing things that you...
zh: 实际上,有时候经验年限反而对你不利,因为你会有一套固定的做事方式,让你……

speaker: Unknown
en: Don't understand how to do more than one agent at a time.
zh: 不明白怎么同时操作多个智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, at this point, you should be relatively comfortable juggling five to 10 ongoing multiple things.
zh: 是的,到这个阶段,你应该能相对从容地同时应付五到十件并行的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's definitely true that you're much more of a manager than an individual contributor.
zh: 而且确实,你更像一个管理者而不是个人贡献者(IC)。

speaker: Unknown
en: I do think that people who look at data rather than code are more valuable these days.
zh: 我确实认为,如今看数据的人比看代码的人更有价值。

speaker: Unknown
en: So being able to say, here's the logs, here's the traces, here's the schema, here's the input output, capturing it, turning it into an eval.
zh: 也就是说,能够说:这是日志、这是 trace、这是 schema、这是输入输出,把它们捕获下来,转化成一个 eval。

speaker: Unknown
en: All these are basically the sort of the merging of AI engineering and ML engineering that is happening that people need to upscale on.
zh: 这些基本上就是 AI 工程和 ML 工程正在发生的融合,是人们需要提升(upskill)的方向。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that the person that has, let's say, 10, 20 years of experience in software engineering really reviews every line and tries to make every line make sense.
zh: 我认为,一个比如说有 10 年、20 年软件工程经验的人,会真的审查每一行代码,试图让每一行都说得通。

speaker: Unknown
en: Whereas now we just need to make the modules make sense.
zh: 而现在我们只需要让模块说得通。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I can allow slop in there because it helps me to go faster as long as I contain the slop in things where I completely understand the whole system.
zh: 我可以容忍里面有垃圾(slop),因为它能帮我跑得更快,只要我把垃圾控制在我完全理解整个系统的东西里。

speaker: Unknown
en: Where you go wrong is you have too many modules, too many black boxes.
zh: 你出错的地方是:模块太多、黑箱太多,

speaker: Unknown
en: where you don't even know and actually the code also gets confused.
zh: 你自己都不知道发生了什么,而且实际上代码本身也会变得混乱。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'm making my own Slack competitor and I saw a bug where the messages weren't loading.
zh: 所以我在做自己的 Slack 竞品,我看到一个 bug:消息加载不出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: I refresh and the messages were loading and I refresh again and the messages were not loading.
zh: 我刷新一下,消息加载出来了;再刷新一下,消息又加载不出来了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's like, well, it's the same exact code, what the hell is going on?
zh: 然后就觉得，明明是完全一样的代码，这到底是怎么回事？

speaker: Unknown
en: Turns out there's two code paths and there's a raised condition.
zh: 结果发现有两条代码路径,存在一个竞态条件(raised condition)。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why?
zh: 为什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: Because two different coding agents worked on it at different times.
zh: 因为两个不同的编码智能体在不同的时间处理过它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And because they just made their own thing.
zh: 而且它们各自造了自己的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So a human would never do that.
zh: 所以人类绝不会那样做。

speaker: Unknown
en: And agents would potentially sometimes do it because sometimes just things fall out of the context window.
zh: 而智能体有时可能会那样做,因为有时候东西就是会掉出上下文窗口。

speaker: Unknown
en: But you need to have the oversight of the module.
zh: 但你需要对模块有监督。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then whatever is inside of the module can be a black box.
zh: 而模块内部的东西可以是黑箱。

speaker: Unknown
en: Prakash asked, which parts of the stack are poorly designed for agents now that agents are becoming the main users of the internet?
zh: Prakash 问:既然智能体正在成为互联网的主要用户,技术栈的哪些部分对智能体来说设计得很糟糕?

speaker: Unknown
en: Compute.
zh: 算力。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everyone knows the GPU shortage.
zh: 人人都知道 GPU 短缺。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everyone knows the memory shortage.
zh: 人人都知道内存短缺。

speaker: Unknown
en: But CPU shortage is the most consistently reported thing among all the people that I interview right now.
zh: 但 CPU 短缺是我现在访谈的所有人当中报告得最一致的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what does that mean?
zh: 那这意味着什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: It does mean that we need sort of more fluid compute, which is the Vercel term for it, more sort of different forms of serverlessness where it's very ephemeral.
zh: 它确实意味着我们需要更流动的算力,这是 Vercel 的说法,也就是更多不同形式的无服务器化,非常 ephemeral 的那种。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can sort of execute and resume because agents need some time to
zh: 你可以执行然后恢复,因为智能体需要一些时间来

speaker: Unknown
en: Do LLM calls or network calls, whatever, but basically long-running states that are resumable.
zh: 做 LLM 调用或网络调用之类的,但本质上是可恢复的长时间运行的状态。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think beyond that, you really start to get into two things which I'm really thinking about, like sort of bandwidth or networking, where the latency starts to really matter.
zh: 但我认为除此之外,你真正开始涉及两件事,我一直在思考的,比如带宽或网络,因为延迟开始真正变得重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's an optimization of like, well, what point of presence are you?
zh: 你在跟什么通信,或者你在哪个区域,对比实际上你应该在云里做多少算力,还是在本地或边缘设备上做?

speaker: Unknown
en: What are you communicating with or what region are you in versus like actually how much compute should you be doing in cloud versus locally or sort of edge devices?
zh: 你在和什么通信，或者你在哪个区域，相对于实际上你应该在云端做多少计算，还是在本地或边缘设备上做？

speaker: Unknown
en: That is definitely happening a lot for the robotics companies that we're talking to.
zh: 这在我们交谈的机器人公司里肯定经常发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: And basically don't treat it as just a robotics problem or the robotics are just the first harbinger of what you guys will eventually be doing if you consume or do enough inference at their scale.
zh: 基本上不要把它仅仅当成一个机器人问题,机器人只是第一个先兆,预示着如果你们的推理量达到他们的规模,你们最终也会做这些事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then finally, to me, on a very, very personal basis, bandwidth.
zh: 最后,对我个人来说,非常重要的就是带宽。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, like, how many tokens per second can I get?
zh: 也就是,我每秒能拿到多少 token?

speaker: Unknown
en: Both on a single call basis, and I just aggregate across all my calls, and then aggregate across my company because I have enough people managing all these calls.
zh: 既看单次调用,也会聚合我所有的调用,然后再聚合到我整个公司,因为我有足够多的人在管理这些调用。

speaker: Unknown
en: SWIX has also been running KillMySass, a bounty for anyone who could replace an events software subscription his company was unhappy paying for.
zh: SWIX 还一直在运行 KillMySass,一项赏金活动,奖励任何能替换掉他公司不愿意继续付费订阅的某款活动软件的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Prakash asked him about it.
zh: Prakash 就此问了他。

speaker: Unknown
en: Basically, you can call this a bounty on mid-tier SaaS that should not exist.
zh: 基本上,你可以把这叫作对不该存在的中端 SaaS 的赏金。

speaker: Unknown
en: Basically, half a salary or one-third of a salary for a piece of software that I don't own that nobody enjoys using.
zh: 基本上,半份薪水或三分之一份薪水,买一款我不拥有、也没人喜欢用的软件。

speaker: Unknown
en: If I'm going to spend $40,000 on this SaaS subscription, I can spend that in amount of tokens, and that buys me a heck of a lot of tokens.
zh: 如果我要在这个 SaaS 订阅上花 4 万美元,我可以把同样多的钱花在 token 上,那能买到一大堆 token。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have so many submissions that we then have to eval them.
zh: 我们收到了太多提交,然后还得对它们做评估。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so evals are the problem.
zh: 所以评估才是问题所在。

speaker: Unknown
en: And because we're no longer checking, there's two or three requirements that you fit.
zh: 因为我们不再是检查你满足两三条要求。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're checking the entire UX of the entire flow from three different perspectives of organizer, attendee, and sponsor, or speaker.
zh: 我们是从组织者、参会者和赞助商或演讲者三个不同视角,检查整个流程的完整用户体验。

speaker: Unknown
en: And just be aware that if you offer a large bounty, like we offered $10,000 as the prize, you get a lot of submissions.
zh: 而且要意识到,如果你提供一大笔赏金,比如我们提供了 1 万美元奖金,你会收到大量提交。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because people want to buy code for fun.
zh: 因为大家想为了乐趣买代码。

speaker: Unknown
en: And a lot of them will be low quality.
zh: 其中很多质量会很低。

speaker: Unknown
en: They will just be like, Claude, make no mistakes.
zh: 它们就是那种:「Claude,别出错。

speaker: Unknown
en: Go do this.
zh: 去把这个做了。」

speaker: Unknown
en: And then they will make mistakes and they'll just submit.
zh: 然后它们会出错,但照样提交。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so like the sort of verification load is very imbalanced because they spent zero thought on this thing.
zh: 所以验证负担是非常不平衡的,因为他们在这些东西上没花一点心思。

speaker: Unknown
en: They just threw it in there.
zh: 他们就是直接扔进去。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you have no idea if it's like low quality or not.
zh: 而你完全不知道它质量是低还是不低。

speaker: Unknown
en: But overall, very successful.
zh: 但总体来说,非常成功。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the team initially, so I have one of the most adversarial non-AI teams in AI.
zh: 至于团队,我拥有 AI 行业里最不迷信 AI(最对抗性)的团队之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, I hire like, what is my business?
zh: 好的,我招的是什么样的人?

speaker: Unknown
en: I hire event professionals who are like super old school.
zh: 我招的是超级老派的活动专业人士。

speaker: Unknown
en: They do everything in spreadsheets.
zh: 他们所有事都用表格做。

speaker: Unknown
en: They work with unions.
zh: 他们跟工会打交道。

speaker: Unknown
en: They have to worry about like placements of like the meter boards physically in like locations, right?
zh: 他们得操心比如展板在各个场地里的实际摆放位置,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Like these are not glamorous, like high tech jobs.
zh: 这些可不是什么光鲜的高科技工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then they're very super suspicious of anything that is new and vibe coded and techy, right?
zh: 所以他们对任何新的、vibe coding 出来的、技术味的东西都非常怀疑,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: So I hire these guys and then I like make them work for AI.
zh: 所以我招了这些人,然后我让他们为 AI 打工。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right?
zh: 对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: That's my job.
zh: 这就是我的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so initially they were like, we'll never use this Vibequoted thing.
zh: 所以一开始他们说,我们绝不会用这个 Vibequoted 的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to use the tried and tested stuff that has been working for Microsoft and all these other guys.
zh: 我要用微软和那些其他家伙一直在用的、久经考验的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then they saw the quality of the submissions.
zh: 然后他们看到了提交的质量。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then they looked at their existing platform.
zh: 然后他们看了看自己现有的平台。

speaker: Unknown
en: They were like, yeah, okay, we're going to switch.
zh: 他们当时就说，好吧，行，我们切换。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like that initial hurdle needs, you basically need to provide the proof of this is feasible.
zh: 就像那个最初的门槛，你基本上需要提供证明，证明这是可行的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the ongoing thing, which is, this is one of the benefits of me partnering with Cognition on, is I just give them, give all of them access to DevIn to modify the code.
zh: 然后是持续的部分，这也是我和 Cognition 合作的好处之一，就是我给他们所有人开放 DevIn 的权限去修改代码。

speaker: Unknown
en: So anything they don't like, they can just request the change and they have it pretty much in one to two hours.
zh: 所以任何他们不喜欢的东西，他们只要请求改动，基本上在一到两个小时内就能搞定。

speaker: Unknown
en: Which they've never had before.
zh: 这在他们以前是从来没有过的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just to give you an idea of the way we work with these SaaS companies, right now, when we request a change, they'll say, OK, that sounds pretty cool.
zh: 给你讲一下我们和这些 SaaS 公司打交道的方式吧，现在，当我们请求一个改动时，他们会说，好，听起来挺不错的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's on our Q3 roadmap.
zh: 它在我们的 Q3 路线图上。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we don't have confidence that it'll actually be done in Q3.
zh: 而我们没有信心它在 Q3 真的能完成。

speaker: Unknown
en: And by the way, we requested for a thing in Q1.
zh: 顺便说一句，我们 Q1 请求的一个东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: It just landed.
zh: 刚刚才上线。

speaker: Unknown
en: So SaaS is quite cooked.
zh: 所以 SaaS 已经相当完蛋了。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you are mostly a CRUD app, I would say that there's a lot of UX issues left.
zh: 如果你主要是一个 CRUD 应用，我会说还剩很多 UX 问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you look at SweetBench and you're like, oh, wow, we're like 90 in SweetBench.
zh: 如果你看 SweetBench 然后说，哦，哇，我们在 SweetBench 上都到 90 了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're looking at the wrong thing, my guy.
zh: 那你看错地方了，我的老兄。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, if you haven't actually tried to completely vibe code a SaaS that you use, you don't understand how models are still very bad at all this.
zh: 你知道吗，如果你没有真正试过完全用 vibe coding 做一个你自己要用的 SaaS，你就无法理解模型在这些事情上仍然非常糟糕。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then I pressed SWIX on the downside.
zh: 然后我按了 SWIX 的负面选项。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I have a hard time seeing how we don't kind of pick a lot of this low hanging fruit and then end up in sort of a lot of companies go out of business.
zh: 但我很难想象我们不会摘掉这大量低垂的果实，最后导致很多公司倒闭。

speaker: Unknown
en: And also I'm thinking like layoffs from like Meta, you know, that's another kind of canary in the coal mine.
zh: 我还在想比如 Meta 的裁员，你知道，那是煤矿里的另一只金丝雀。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, are we going to see mass layoffs from big tech?
zh: 比如，我们会看到大科技公司的大规模裁员吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: How long can the party go on?
zh: 这场派对还能持续多久？

speaker: Unknown
en: The simple answer is if you look at it as a fixed part of software engineering, then that is the conclusion that you will arrive at.
zh: 简单的回答是，如果你把它看作软件工程中一个固定的部分，那你就会得出那个结论。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if you look at it as the point of my competition or my TAM is spreadsheets.
zh: 但如果你把它看作，我的竞争或我的 TAM 的对手是电子表格。

speaker: Unknown
en: All spreadsheets made by anyone with any sort of productivity tooling can be turned into custom software for them to put on Rails and with a beautiful UX and with automations.
zh: 所有拥有任何生产力工具的人做出来的电子表格，都可以被转化为定制软件，让他们走上正轨，配上漂亮的 UX 和自动化。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then the demand for custom software becomes a lot larger.
zh: 那么对定制软件的需求就会大得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And more beyond that, if it's phone calls, if it's emails that go back and forth and eventually physical meetings between people,
zh: 除此之外，如果是电话，如果是来回往复的邮件，以及最终人与人之间的线下会面，

speaker: Unknown
en: All of that can be incrementally turned into more and more and more and more customer software and hardware and models right away.
zh: 所有这些都可以逐步被转化为越来越多的客户软件、硬件和模型，立刻就可以。

speaker: Unknown
en: Basically, we're just growing into the long tail.
zh: 基本上，我们只是在向长尾增长。
